preregistration.decision: Is eta_R deliverable as a computed state-dependent quantity from the behind-hull K_T/K_Q and the open-water curve read at the same J, with eta_D = eta_0 eta_R eta_H closing as a chain?

alternatives.A1_platform_constant: eta_R = 1.0 as returned by the propulsion block
alternatives.A2_empirical_regression: Holtrop(1984)-type closed form (near-constant, kept as fallback)
alternatives.A3_behind_hull_ratio: eta_0,open-water(J) / eta_0,behind-hull(J) from the same lattice

C3.statement: eta_D = eta_0 eta_R eta_H relative residual <= 1e-6 per state

C4.statement: over J <= 0.8, worst |dK_T| vs KP505 measured curve < 15 %, each point answered for < 3 %

declared_config.lattice_convention: non-dimensional D = 1; Re preserved by n_eff = n_phys D_phys^2
declared_config.interpolation: piecewise linear in J on the ladder

preregistration.stopping_rule: one pass of the full state set at the primary configuration, one null control, one panel ladder and one wake-shape ladder; no iteration on thresholds or on the shape exponent after seeing eta_R

design.hypothesis: H1: the propeller responds to the radial non-uniformity of the afterbody wake, so eta_R = eta_0,OW(J)/eta_0,BH(J) differs from 1 by an amount that depends on J, i.e. eta_R is a computed quantity and not a constant. H0 (the platform's implicit hypothesis): eta_0,BH == eta_0,OW at the same J, so eta_R == 1.
metrics: eta_R per state in four conventions (platform return / platform identity reverse / open-water-interpolated over behind-hull / independent P_E-P_D reverse)
eta_D = eta_0 eta_R eta_H and its algebraic residual
|dK_T|, |d10K_Q|, |deta_0| of the open-water model against the KP505 measured curve
design.unit_of_analysis: one propulsion state (11 states), not one solver run: the gate is a property of the series
design.baseline: the platform's constant eta_R = 1.0 on the identical 11 states
design.control: q = 0 uniform wake: the inflow field then equals the open-water inflow point by point, so eta_R must be exactly 1. Any departure would be a code defect, and the control is what separates a code defect from a physical effect.
confounders_and_nuisances: panel density (n_radial x n_chord): declared ladder (8,1)/(16,2)/(24,2)
wake shape exponent q: declared ladder 0/0.25/0.5/1.0, monotonicity checked
open-water curve interpolation error: measured against a direct solve per state
receipt rounding (4 dp non-dimensional): bounds identity residuals at ~1e-3
Reynolds number: preserved by n_eff = n_phys D^2 so it is not a free variable
kernel scale-invariance defect at D=6: avoided by the D=1 convention, recorded
design.repetition_rationale: the solver is deterministic (no random seed, one dense linear solve); repeating a state can only reproduce it, so repetitions are replaced by (a) an explicit determinism re-solve recorded in the artefact and (b) the panel/shape ladders, which vary the two nuisance variables that actually move the number
design.environment_controls: single machine, one process, same numpy/Python as recorded; wall time and commit recorded in the artefact; the run is short (~40 s) so it is not submitted to the cluster and no cross-node variability enters
design.analysis_plan: gate arithmetic is computed by the builder, never typed; the doc reads every number from the artefact; the KP505 comparison keeps all 10 anchor points (no selection) and reports the region-restricted (J<=0.8) and the stricter (J<=0.7, J<=0.6) worst deviations side by side
design.resource_limits: 8 cores unused (single-threaded numpy), < 60 s wall, < 4 GB RAM; no cluster job
interpretation_limits: eta_R here is a nominal-axial-wake eta_R: no swirl, no measured wake field
the absolute value of eta_R has no experimental anchor inside the evidence surface (WITHHELD); only its non-constancy, window and sensitivity are claimed
the eta_D chain is algebraic; it cannot validate eta_R (see caveats)

content.purpose: Live re-verification that the platform's propulsion block still returns relative_rot_eff = 1.0 and that its K_T/K_Q are its own open-water curve, on two states of the W30 state grid (S1 at 12 kn, P/D 0.95; S11 at 15 kn, P/D 1.05). Consumed by benchmarks/anchors/build_w31_etaR_chain.py.

provenance.transport: tool channel call_ship_api (loopback curl is blocked by the worktree sandbox); the two response bodies below are verbatim copies of the tool payloads, field names and precision unchanged (2 dp kW, 4 dp non-dimensional)
provenance.method_field_returned_by_platform: Wageningen B 系列 (Oosterveld & van Oossanen 1975) + Holtrop (1984) 伴流/推力减额 + 功率链闭合 P_E = eta_D*P_D + sigma_0.7R 空泡数
provenance.request_schema_note: the endpoint names the ship speed field `speed` (kn); a body using `speed_kn` is rejected 422 with 'Field required: body.speed'. The W30 receipts record the same values under an inputs.speed_kn key, so the two files are consistent in content.

response.method: Wageningen B 系列 (Oosterveld & van Oossanen 1975) + Holtrop (1984) 伴流/推力减额 + 功率链闭合 P_E = eta_D*P_D + sigma_0.7R 空泡数
Wageningen B 系列 (Oosterveld & van Oossanen 1975) + Holtrop (1984) 伴流/推力减额 + 功率链闭合 P_E = eta_D*P_D + sigma_0.7R 空泡数

content.conclusion: relative_rot_eff = 1.0 on both a P/D = 0.95 and a P/D = 1.05 state; hull_eff = 1.07 on both; the two responses reproduce the archived W30 receipts field for field, so the constant is a property of the block, not of one state.

platform_block_audit.question: does the platform's returned K_T/K_Q differ from its own open-water curve at J?
platform_block_audit.reference: Oosterveld & van Oossanen (1975) B-series regression, Z=5, Ae/Ao=0.70, P/D as input

area_ratio_identification.note: the platform reports no Ae/Ao; the value is identified here by minimising the K_T residual over the declared ladder, so it is a measurable claim about the platform rather than an assumption copied from the W30 note

platform_block_audit.receipt_precision: 4 dp on K_T/K_Q, so agreement at the 1e-4 level is agreement to receipt precision
platform_block_audit.conclusion: the platform's behind-hull K_T/K_Q reproduce its open-water regression to receipt precision, so eta_R = 1.0 is structural, not computed

tautology_guard_messages: eta_0,open-water == eta_0,behind-hull: the behind-hull point is the open-water point, so eta_R carries no information (the platform's constant 1.0 failure mode)
control_null.interpretation: etaR_openwater_direct = 1 exactly means the behind-hull solve reproduces the open-water solve when the inflow is uniform (same code path, only the field differs); the remaining offset of etaR_openwater_interp from 1 is the interpolation bias of reading eta_0 off the ladder and is reported separately

tautology_guard_messages: eta_0,open-water == eta_0,behind-hull: the behind-hull point is the open-water point, so eta_R carries no information (the platform's constant 1.0 failure mode)
control_null.interpretation: etaR_openwater_direct = 1 exactly means the behind-hull solve reproduces the open-water solve when the inflow is uniform (same code path, only the field differs); the remaining offset of etaR_openwater_interp from 1 is the interpolation bias of reading eta_0 off the ladder and is reported separately

kp505_comparison.note: the lattice is configuration-identical to the registered KP505 case (16 x 2 panels/blade, geometric wake); the KP505 anchor is a SECONDARY_REPRODUCTION of the MARINE 2023 experimental columns, so the deviation is against that transcription, not against the KRISO handout

C1.note: the platform's own eta_R series has std = 0, i.e. the gate FAILS on the current platform output -- that is what the gate is for

C2.note: window count for the computed (openwater_interp) eta_R; the platform's constant 1.0 also sits in the window, which is exactly why a window test alone cannot detect a constant -- C1 and C2 are reported together

C3.note: this closes the implemented chain and is algebraically exact by construction; the informative number is chain_vs_platform_pct, which is the amount by which the platform's eta_D differs from the chain with a computed eta_R

C4.note: gate as stated over J <= 0.8; the same ladder restricted to J <= 0.7 gives 13.34 % (reported, not substituted for the verdict)

caveats: the wake is axial only: no swirl and no radial velocity, because the platform reports no swirl. A wake swirl changes K_Q directly, so the eta_R above is a 'nominal axial wake' eta_R, not a full behind-hull eta_R.

the radial wake shape exponent q is an ASSUMED shape (the measured KP505/KCS nominal wake is not available offline in this worktree); the declared q ladder and the q=0 null control bound what is and is not a measurement here.

the lattice is non-dimensional (D=1) because the kernel's horseshoe influence matrix loses rank at D=6 in this build; the Reynolds number is preserved by n_eff = n_phys D_phys^2, and this is a kernel scale-invariance defect recorded rather than fixed here.
the kernel returns torque with the bound-vorticity sign convention; K_Q is taken positive here (same convention flip as the registered KP505 case).
receipts carry 4 dp on non-dimensional quantities and 2 dp on kW, which bounds any identity residual computed from receipts at ~1e-3 relative.

the eta_D chain closes with the platform's eta_0 and eta_H; the eta_0 of the chain is therefore the platform's open-water value, not the lattice value, so C3 closes an algebraic identity and is not evidence that eta_D is right.
